# Knights of the Frozen Throne

Knights of the Frozen Throne
Input file: standard input
Output file: standard output
Time limit: 2 seconds
Memory limit: 1024 megabytes
Knights of the Frozen Throne is a famous online game developed and published by ICPC Entertainment,
Inc.
A single server called Zeus Super Computer (ZSC) handles all requests from all players of the game.
Originally, all players’ data is stored in ZSC’s memory so that the server can respond to a request without
querying the database. However, this design hardly scales as the game becomes more and more popular.
As a great engineer in ICPC Entertainment, Tom wants to help the company save costs by using an
awesome database with a very large capacity. After some investigation, Tom discovers the behavior
patterns of all players, and he can accurately predict when a player will send a request. Now it’s time to
deploy his optimization design: time-based caching.
To introduce the time-based caching policy, instead of holding all players’ data in memory all the time,
a player’s data is retained in memory only for a while, and ZSC will drop this player’s data if he doesn’t
send any request for some time. Specifically, when the request from one player comes,
• if the player’s data is not in memory, ZSC loads his data into memory and records the last request
time of the player;
• if the player’s data is already in memory, ZSC responds to this request immediately, then updates
the last request time of the player.
Also, ZSC would drop a player’s data from memory if X seconds (X is a positive integer parameter to
be determined) have elapsed since his last request. In particular, if a request is sent exactly X seconds
after the player’s last request time, ZSC does have to load the player’s data into memory. Initially, ZSC’s
memory is empty.
Tom wants you to help him determine the best positive integer X such that the total cost is minimized.
As for the cost of CPU and memory, it costs a dollars for ZSC to hold one player’s data in memory for
one second. ZSC’s CPU is pretty powerful, and it costs i · bi
if i players’ data is loaded in one second.
Input
The input starts with a line of a single integer m (1 ≤ m ≤ 105
), indicating the number of game players.
Then follow m lines, specifying the predicted requests of the players. Each of them begins with a single
integer k (1 ≤ k ≤ 5 × 105
), denoting the number of requests player i will send. The remaining k integers
p1, p2, · · · , pk (1 ≤ p1 ≤ p2 ≤ · · · ≤ pk ≤ 109
) are the times(in second) predicted by Tom that the player
will send request to ZSC. It is guaranteed that the total number of requests sent by all players does not
exceed 5 × 105
.
The next line contains an integer a (1 ≤ a ≤ 104
), the cost for ZSC to hold one player’s data in memory
for one second.
The last line contains m integers b1, b2, · · · , bm (1 ≤ bi ≤ 109
), the cost of loading one player’s data if i
players’ data is loaded in one second.
Output
Print two integers in the first line, denoting the minimum total cost and the number of different positive
integers X that can achieve this minimum cost. Then list all these values of X in increasing order in the
second line.
Page 1 of 2

It can be proved that there are finitely many different positive integers X, such that the total cost is
minimized.
Examples
standard input standard output
4
3 1 4 5
2 2 4
4 2 4 7 8
6 1 3 5 7 8 10
1
2 4 6 5
53 2
3 4
3
3 1 1 4
5 1 4 4 5 7
3 3 4 5
2
6 4 3
55 1
1
Note
The total cost of different values of X is shown in Figure 1.
Рис. 1: The first sample data.
Page 2 of 2

# Knights of the Frozen Throne

Time limit: $2$ seconds. Memory limit: $1024$ MB. Standard input and standard output.

Knights of the Frozen Throne is a popular online game developed by ICPC Entertainment, Inc.

A single server, the Zeus Super Computer (ZSC), handles every player's requests. Initially the design keeps all player data in memory so requests can be answered without database queries. This design becomes difficult to scale as the game grows more popular.

Engineer Tom proposes using a very large database to reduce costs. After studying the players' behavior, he can accurately predict when each player will send requests. He now wants to implement time-based caching.

A player's data stays in memory only temporarily. When a request arrives:

- If that player's data is absent, ZSC loads it into memory and records the last request time.
- If the data is already in memory, ZSC answers immediately and updates the last request time.

ZSC removes the data when $X$ seconds have elapsed since that player's last request, where $X$ is a positive integer to be chosen. In particular, a request arriving exactly $X$ seconds after the previous request requires the data to be loaded again. The memory is initially empty.

Choose a positive integer $X$ minimizing the total cost. Keeping one player's data in memory for one second costs $a$ dollars. If the data of $i$ players is loaded during the same second, the total CPU cost for those loads is $i\cdot b_i$.

## Input

The first line contains $m$ ($1\leq m\leq10^5$), the number of players.

Each of the next $m$ lines describes one player's requests. It starts with $k$ ($1\leq k\leq5\times10^5$), followed by $k$ integers $p_1,p_2,\ldots,p_k$ ($1\leq p_1\leq p_2\leq\cdots\leq p_k\leq10^9$), the request times in seconds. The total number of requests over all players does not exceed $5\times10^5$.

The next line contains $a$ ($1\leq a\leq10^4$), the memory cost for one player for one second.

The last line contains $m$ integers $b_1,b_2,\ldots,b_m$ ($1\leq b_i\leq10^9$). If $i$ players' data is loaded during one second, each player's load costs $b_i$.

## Output

On the first line, print two integers: the minimum total cost and the number of positive integers $X$ attaining it. On the second line, print all such $X$ in increasing order.

It can be proved that only finitely many positive integers $X$ attain the minimum.

## Note

The figure shows the total cost for different $X$ in the first example.

![diagram](frozen-throne-cost.png)

# Knights of the Frozen Throne

时间限制：$2$ 秒。内存限制：$1024$ MB。使用标准输入和标准输出。

《冰封王座的骑士》是由 ICPC 娱乐公司开发并发行的一款热门网络游戏。

一台名为宙斯超级计算机（ZSC）的服务器处理所有玩家的请求。原来的设计将所有玩家的数据都存放在内存中，从而无需查询数据库就能响应请求。但随着游戏越来越受欢迎，这种设计很难继续扩展。

工程师 Tom 希望使用一个容量很大的数据库来节省成本。经过研究，他掌握了玩家的行为规律，可以准确预测每个玩家何时会发送请求。现在，他准备部署一种按时间淘汰的缓存方案。

每个玩家的数据只在内存中保留一段时间。收到请求时：

- 如果该玩家的数据不在内存中，ZSC 会将其载入内存，并记录该玩家最近一次请求的时间。
- 如果数据已经在内存中，ZSC 会立即响应请求，然后更新该玩家最近一次请求的时间。

自某个玩家上次请求起经过 $X$ 秒后，ZSC 就会将其数据移出内存，其中 $X$ 是待确定的正整数。特别地，如果请求恰好在上次请求的 $X$ 秒后到达，就必须重新载入数据。内存最初为空。

请选出使总成本最小的正整数 $X$。将一位玩家的数据在内存中保留一秒，费用为 $a$ 美元。如果同一秒内载入了 $i$ 位玩家的数据，这些载入操作的 CPU 总费用为 $i\cdot b_i$。

## 输入

第一行包含整数 $m$（$1\leq m\leq10^5$），表示玩家数。

接下来 $m$ 行，每行描述一位玩家的请求：先给出整数 $k$（$1\leq k\leq5\times10^5$），再给出 $k$ 个整数 $p_1,p_2,\ldots,p_k$（$1\leq p_1\leq p_2\leq\cdots\leq p_k\leq10^9$），表示请求发生的时刻，单位为秒。保证所有玩家的请求总数不超过 $5\times10^5$。

下一行包含整数 $a$（$1\leq a\leq10^4$），表示将一位玩家的数据保留在内存中一秒的费用。

最后一行包含 $m$ 个整数 $b_1,b_2,\ldots,b_m$（$1\leq b_i\leq10^9$）。若同一秒载入 $i$ 位玩家的数据，则其中每位玩家的数据载入费用为 $b_i$。

## 输出

第一行输出两个整数：最小总成本，以及能达到该成本的正整数 $X$ 的个数。第二行按递增顺序输出所有这样的 $X$。

可以证明，使总成本达到最小的正整数 $X$ 只有有限多个。

## 说明

下图展示了第一组样例在不同 $X$ 下的总成本。

![diagram](frozen-throne-cost.png)
